title: PanelCOMP Class
summary: Official Derivative Python API reference for PanelCOMP instances, covering panel value access, panel hierarchy, pixel bounds, drop readiness, virtual mouse/touch interaction, mouse location, focus control, and inherited COMP behavior.
guidance: Use this article when scripting Panel Component state, hierarchy, dimensions, virtual interactions, drag/drop readiness, mouse coordinates, or focus.
Access panel values through the panel member, for example op('button1').panel.u.val, when code needs Python-side PanelValue state.
Use panelRoot, panelChildren, and panelParent(n) to reason about the panel hierarchy; panelParent(n) climbs input-panel parenting first and then containing-panel hierarchy.
interactMouse() updates inside, insideu, insidev, state, u, and v up the parent chain; the first primary mouse down or touch on a panel takes precedence over later touches and hovers.

interactMouse() uses normalized coordinates by default; set pixels=True for pixel offsets or screen=True for screen-relative coordinates, and set quiet=False when warnings about conflicting interaction state are useful.
Use interactTouch(), interactClear(), and interactStatus() when multiple virtual touches or hover states need to be simulated and inspected.
Use locateMouse() or locateMouseUV() only when the mouse is over a window containing the panel; otherwise they can return None.
setFocus() sets hierarchical focus and the focusselect panel value when the panel is open.
Read dropReady before assuming a drop operation will be accepted by the current panel.
